Class LessonInputPolicy

java.lang.Object
validation.LessonInputPolicy
public class LessonInputPolicy extends Object

Title: LessonInputPolicy Class

Description: Holds the checks applied to the fields of a lesson learned before that lesson is written to the database, in the order they are applied. It is the lessons learned counterpart of the supplied ScreenInputPolicy class and follows the same shape: a small Problem record describing one refused input, and a method per field that returns the first problem it finds or null when the input is acceptable.

The limits live here rather than being scattered through the create and update code so that the create path and the update path cannot drift apart. Both call validateLesson, so a lesson that would be refused on the way in cannot slip through on an edit (Contributor story CS-7). Length is always checked before anything else, for the reason given in InputLimits: a single long paste should be refused cheaply before any other work is done on it (CS-11).

This class has no JavaFX reference and does no database work, so the testing automation can exercise every rule directly.

      public static final String RESERVED_CATEGORY
      The label the list page's category filter uses for "do not filter by category". It is defined here, not in the GUI, so the rule that refuses it as a category and the filter that offers it share one value; guiLessonsList.ModelLessonsList.ALL_CATEGORIES refers to it.

    • LONG_TEXT_ABSOLUTE_MAX

      public static final int LONG_TEXT_ABSOLUTE_MAX
      The cheap ceiling for the two long text fields.

      TP2 correction. In HW2 the description and the resolution were checked with InputLimits.checkLength, which applies InputLimits.ABSOLUTE_MAX of 256 characters before it looks at the field's own limit. The result was that any description longer than 256 characters was refused as "far too long", even though the stated limit was 2000. This was found while writing the TP2 boundary tests: a 2000 character description, which the documentation said was acceptable, was refused. The long fields now have their own, larger ceiling, so a huge paste is still refused cheaply but a real lesson is not.

      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • validateLesson

      public static LessonInputPolicy.Problem validateLesson(String title, String category, String description, String resolution, String keywords, String contributor)

      Method: Problem validateLesson(String title, String category, String description, String resolution, String keywords, String contributor)

      Description: Checks every field of a lesson in a fixed order, used by both the create and the update operations. The order is the order the fields appear on the lesson editor screen, so the first problem a user is told about is the first field they would read.

      Parameters:
      title - the heading the user typed
      category - the category the user typed
      description - the body of the lesson
      resolution - the reply that resolved the lesson, which may be empty
      keywords - the comma separated keywords, which may be empty
      contributor - the username contributing the lesson
      Returns:
      null when every field is acceptable, otherwise the first problem found

    • validateTitle

      public static LessonInputPolicy.Problem validateTitle(String title)

      Method: Problem validateTitle(String title)

      Description: The title is required because it is the part of a lesson shown in the list, so a lesson with no title could not be told apart from another (CS-10). A title made only of spaces is treated as empty, because it would show as a blank line in the list.

      Parameters:
      title - the heading the user typed
      Returns:
      null when the title is acceptable, otherwise the problem found

    • validateCategory

      public static LessonInputPolicy.Problem validateCategory(String category)

      Method: Problem validateCategory(String category)

      Description: The category is required because the filter by category (CS-5) has nothing to group a lesson under if it is blank. RESERVED_CATEGORY is refused, ignoring case and surrounding spaces, because the filter treats it as "every category", so a lesson stored under it could never be shown on its own.

      Parameters:
      category - the category the user typed
      Returns:
      null when the category is acceptable, otherwise the problem found

    • validateKeywords

      public static LessonInputPolicy.Problem validateKeywords(String keywords)

      Method: Problem validateKeywords(String keywords)

      Description: Keywords are optional. When they are given they must be a comma separated list of at most MAX_KEYWORD_COUNT words, each no longer than MAX_ONE_KEYWORD characters and made only of letters, digits, spaces, hyphens, full stops, and plus signs. The character rule exists because keywords are matched by the search (CS-4); punctuation such as a semicolon is almost always a mistyped separator, and a keyword containing one would never be matched by what a user types. The plus sign and the full stop are allowed so that names such as C++ and Node.js can be keywords.

      Parameters:
      keywords - the comma separated keywords, which may be empty
      Returns:
      null when the keywords are acceptable, otherwise the problem found

    • validateDescription

      public static LessonInputPolicy.Problem validateDescription(String description)

      Method: Problem validateDescription(String description)

      Description: The description is required because it holds the actual lesson. A lesson with a title and nothing else records that something happened but not what (CS-10).

      Parameters:
      description - the body the user typed
      Returns:
      null when the description is acceptable, otherwise the problem found

    • validateResolution

      public static LessonInputPolicy.Problem validateResolution(String resolution)

      Method: Problem validateResolution(String resolution)

      Description: The resolution is optional, because a lesson can be recorded before anyone has resolved it, in the same way an Ed Discussion question can sit for a while before it is answered. When it is left blank it is accepted; when it is filled in it still has to be within the length limit (CS-11).

      Parameters:
      resolution - the reply the user typed, which may be empty
      Returns:
      null when the resolution is acceptable, otherwise the problem found

    • validateContributor

      public static LessonInputPolicy.Problem validateContributor(String contributor)

      Method: Problem validateContributor(String contributor)

      Description: The contributor is required because a lesson with no author cannot be credited, and the ownership rule (CS-9) has nothing to compare against. In TP2 the screens fill this in from the logged in account rather than letting the user type it, so this check guards against a programming error rather than a typing error.

      Parameters:
      contributor - the username of the contributor
      Returns:
      null when the contributor is acceptable, otherwise the problem found

    • checkLongText

      public static String checkLongText(String input, int maxLength, String fieldName)

      Method: String checkLongText(String input, int maxLength, String fieldName)

      Description: The length check for the two long text fields. It works the same way as InputLimits.checkLength, a cheap ceiling first and then the field's own limit, but with a ceiling large enough for a real lesson. See LONG_TEXT_ABSOLUTE_MAX for why this exists.

      Parameters:
      input - the text the user typed; null is treated as empty
      maxLength - the limit for this field
      fieldName - the name shown to the user in the message
      Returns:
      an empty string when the length is acceptable, otherwise the message to show

    • isBlank

      public static boolean isBlank(String input)

      Method: boolean isBlank(String input)

      Description: True when the input is null, empty, or only spaces. The HW2 version used InputLimits.isEmpty, which accepted a title of three spaces; that would appear in the list as a blank line, which is the exact problem the required field rule exists to prevent.

      Parameters:
      input - the text to examine
      Returns:
      true when there is nothing but white space in the input
